title: Prospective fourth-level Reference refinement and first-order Richardson-limit confirmation

trigger.observation: All 30 material-component Reference sequences converged, while mid-fine Reference self-difference remained approximately equal to the DOP853-to-fine-Reference residual.
trigger.reason: Test the newly exposed first-order finite-Reference truncation hypothesis prospectively before any closure/model-form attribution.

scope.bottom_boundary: zero prescribed pressure head at fixed 160 cm
scope.candidate: unchanged R16_OP equal-grid Layer-ROM DOP853 oracle

hypothesis.temporal_model: For each common observable, finite Reference error is asymptotically first order in outer interval dt over the tested levels.
hypothesis.prediction: REF_DT_1P25E4 should lie near the first-order prediction R_fine + 0.5*(R_fine-R_mid), and DOP853 should lie near the first-order Richardson limit 2*R_ultra-R_fine.
hypothesis.interpretation: This is a temporal-axis hypothesis only; it does not assert physical equivalence or application acceptance.

common_observables: QAVG_cm_per_day over each 0.001 d observation interval
QEND_cm_per_day at the common observation endpoint

frozen_diagnostics.holdout_first_order_ratio: report fine-ultra RMS / mid-fine RMS; expected asymptotic value 0.5
frozen_diagnostics.observed_order: log2(mid-fine RMS / fine-ultra RMS), diagnostic only
frozen_diagnostics.first_order_holdout_prediction: pointwise predicted ultra = fine + 0.5*(fine-mid); compare predicted ultra to actual ultra
frozen_diagnostics.richardson_limit: pointwise R_star = 2*ultra - fine; compare DOP853 to R_star

gates.material_supported: all five components satisfy all four per-component gates

next_if_supported: Treat the R16_OP equal-grid residual as Reference temporal truncation at the finite B1H/B1HCK step sizes, then rebase reduced L4/L6/R8 fixed-head fidelity against a temporally qualified Reference before any model-form claim.
next_if_mixed: Remain on the Reference temporal/operator axis for only the failing material-component mechanisms; do not redesign Layer-ROM state or closure.
